title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A Georgia couple lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that used an AI-generated fake website to display false investment balances. The scammer initiated contact via WhatsApp and persuaded the victim to use a legitimate mobile trading app, but criminals intercepted what appeared on his screen to show fabricated gains and allow small withdrawals that built false confidence in the scheme.

This is a case of a legitimate tool, the trading app, being subverted outside its design context by attackers who controlled what information the user saw. The deception succeeded because the victim had no way to verify that the balances displayed were real without independent confirmation from the app provider or financial institution. What would have prevented the loss is not established, but police indicated that victims in similar cases rarely recover funds once the money leaves their control.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest using a mobile trading app, gradually increasing the amounts while allowing small withdrawals to build trust. Unknown to Jerry, scammers had created an artificial intelligence-generated fake website that displayed false investment balances on his screen. When Jerry tried to withdraw a larger sum last week, he discovered the money was gone and contacted police.

The Gwinnett County couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, are now warning others about the sophisticated tactics used by scammers. Police confirmed the trading app itself was legitimate, but criminals had manipulated what appeared on Jerry's screen to show fake gains. Investigators indicated that victims in similar cases rarely recover their stolen funds. The couple's children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help them manage daily expenses as they work with police on the investigation.
